discovery: Photonic crystals and the photonic band gap: control of light emission and propagation in periodic dielectric structures
motivation: In 1987 Yablonovitch and John independently proposed that periodic dielectric structures can have a complete photonic band gap. Yablonovitch's version inhibits spontaneous emission. John's localizes light. The idea changed a basic assumption: the vacuum's electromagnetic modes, and with them light-matter interaction, can be engineered. Yablonovitch went on to demonstrate the first three-dimensional band-gap structure. Noda turned the concept into rigorous experimental reality. He realized full three-dimensional photonic crystals, ultrahigh-Q nanocavities and controlled spontaneous emission. He also created the photonic-crystal surface-emitting laser, now a high-power, single-mode semiconductor light source on its way to industrial use. Together their work founded modern nanophotonics. It underpins slow light, quantum-dot cavity QED and single-photon sources, as well as nanolasers, energy-efficient on-chip optical interconnects and inverse-designed cavities that confine light far below the diffraction limit. This is a fundamental physics concept that also delivers practical technology.
